entries.claim: Dragging Movements (AA) requires that all functionality using a dragging movement be achievable by a single pointer without dragging unless dragging is essential; the design surface is a dragging interface, so the editor itself fails AA without select-then-click, arrow nudge and span steppers.
source_refs: prd:13.2 (quotes the specification understanding page verbatim)
entries.notes: [V] Quoted verbatim in the source. Applies to the tool's own UI, separately from published output.

entries.claim: Target Size (AA) requires a 24x24 CSS px minimum with four exceptions; award-style editor chrome (thin handles, tiny grips, dense icon rows) violates it by default and needs a live bounding-rect check on render, not only at lock.

Automated accessibility testing catches 57.38% of real issues, measured across 13,000+ pages/page-states and roughly 300,000 issues; therefore the honest claim is 'passed N automated and structural gates', never a conformance claim.
entries.notes: [V] Load-bearing for the disclosure wording and for refusing any conformance claim anywhere in product copy or the evidence bundle.

entries.claim: The perceptual contrast model is a candidate for the next accessibility guideline generation, is still draft, and has no independent legal standing today; the defensible posture is a dual gate that passes the legally standing ratios and computes the perceptual value as a stricter internal target.
entries.notes: [V] for the draft status. The specific perceptual bands are separately flagged unverified - see EL-005.

entries.claim: The specific perceptual contrast bands used as stretch targets were inherited from a prior report and not independently re-verified in the source pass.
entries.notes: [U] Use as a stretch target only; the legally standing ratio remains the pass/fail gate. Re-verify before any gate depends on the exact numbers.

entries.claim: Core Web Vitals thresholds are LCP <= 2.5s, CLS <= 0.1 and INP <= 200ms at the 75th percentile; the responsiveness metric replaced its predecessor in March 2024 and is now the most commonly failed vital, and only a minority of mobile origins pass all three.
entries.notes: [V] Main-thread cost from motion is therefore a live risk, not theoretical.

entries.claim: The canonical performance gate is a median-of-three mobile run under a documented slow-network plus CPU-throttling profile, with LCP, CLS and INP thresholds plus a pre-render transfer budget stated as a range; two acceptance criteria elsewhere in the source are recorded as inconsistent with it (one omits the responsiveness metric, one states a flat transfer figure).
entries.notes: [V] The inconsistency is recorded in the source itself as requiring a cross-section edit. Adopted here as NA-16.

entries.claim: Container queries, relational selectors, registered custom properties, cascade layers, nesting and logical properties are baseline widely available; subgrid is universally supported; anchor positioning remains a carryover interoperability item and must not carry load-bearing layout.
entries.notes: [V] This platform fact is why sibling-anchored free positioning is deferred rather than shipped, and why component internals key off container queries.

entries.claim: Three shipped builders implement a one-direction (larger-to-smaller) breakpoint cascade and work; the one that ships a separate mobile grid with independent block placement has a documented overlap epidemic in which text boxes overlap and blocks change order and position.
entries.notes: [V] Verdict adopted: desktop-down cascade with sparse overrides, never two independent layouts.

entries.claim: A block with no small-breakpoint override compiles to full width in source order; that single default prevents the overlap half of the documented small-screen failure.
entries.notes: [V] Reachable only because overrides attach downward.

entries.claim: The design-tool constraint model this layout contract is modelled on is explicit that its two positioning systems do not mix, and that the escape hatch is a single per-child toggle that removes one child from flow while keeping it inside the parent.
entries.notes: [V] A second major design tool copied the same shape.

entries.claim: Drawing the gridline overlay by reading the section's resolved template columns makes drag an integer-rounding problem and makes the persisted value inherently fluid, so the design surface and the export consume the same data.
entries.notes: [V] Corollary: if the grid is only an overlay and snapped positions bake as margins, then snap-to-gridline is decoration and a later grid change reflows nothing.

entries.claim: A shipped commercial grid editor validates the approach with arbitrary row and column counts, several unit types, placement by clicking a cell or typing numbers, and explicit multi-cell spanning.
entries.notes: [V] Independent market validation that integer grid placement is a workable authoring model.

entries.claim: Naive absolute positioning as a free-position implementation removes the element from flow so an auto-height parent collapses, bakes in the authoring viewport width, and leaves the element off-screen or in dead space at other widths; practitioner documentation for two products states the cost bluntly.
entries.notes: [V] Hence anchored offset with a reserved minimum block size, per-breakpoint scope, an authored flow fallback and a hard lock gate.

entries.claim: For artwork whose composition depends on absolute relationships across the whole viewport, the only workable answer is to treat the composition as one component with internal responsive rules, which means the user cannot drag its parts individually.
entries.notes: [V] Recorded in the source as having no better answer. This is a product limitation, not a defect to fix later.

entries.claim: A same-origin preview frame is required because a scaled element cannot evaluate media queries against a simulated width; the trap is that shipped viewport defaults use automatic height, so any viewport-height rule measures the expanded frame and hero framing looks right in the editor and wrong on device.
entries.notes: [V] Fix adopted: pin real device sizes for both the frame and the capture window, and assert the measured height.

entries.claim: Injected wrappers for hit-testing change what child, first-child and gap selectors match, so removing them at export silently shifts spacing with no explicable cause; the alternative is attributes on elements that already exist plus a single sibling overlay outside the layout root.
entries.notes: [V] Stated in the source as an architectural constraint, not a note. Makes removal at lock provably a no-op.

entries.claim: Reconstructing a document from rendered markup is lossy exactly at anchors, variants and intent, and is the canonical editor failure; it is worse here because an AI agent also writes that source, so the next read sees reformatted markup with its own comments gone.
entries.notes: [V] Prior art splits into JSON-document-plus-pure-render families and files-as-truth-with-annotation families; the former is adopted.

entries.claim: Two shipped visual products are one-way doors: one drops several content and platform features on export, the other ships no markup export at all; a reversible export is therefore a differentiating requirement rather than table stakes.
entries.notes: [V] Directly motivates the settled reversibility decision.

entries.claim: Export must be a re-render with the editor disabled, never a copy-and-strip; the first-party precedent for copy-and-strip required rewriting every path prefix and manually excluding development pages from the shipped folder.
entries.notes: [V] First-party file read. This is the leakage the settled export decision exists to prevent.

entries.claim: Five layered mechanisms keep the editor out of the publish build graph: separate configs, commands and output directories; command-gated development-only injection; a toolbar class of UI that cannot appear in published output; statically replaced environment guards that must be explicitly defined false because an undefined variable may not be tree-shaken; and a post-build hook that scrubs then asserts.
source_refs: prd:12.5 (framework documentation plus a filed bundler issue)
entries.notes: [V] The undefined-variable tree-shaking gotcha is real and filed; it is the reason the guard is explicitly defined rather than merely absent.

entries.claim: There are eight purity gates, not five: the three added are zero unresolved references with no unacknowledged migration flags, zero design-time origins anywhere in emitted output, and a verify-clean check that also re-serialises every document into canonical form.
entries.notes: [V] The source records the consequential cross-section edits it cannot make itself. Carried as NA-03.

entries.claim: A hardcoded design-time origin in an image reference passes the editor-string, size, screenshot and interaction gates and then fails for every visitor; the origins grep must cover source sets, meta content, inline styles, stylesheet urls and imports, structured data and sourcemap comments.
entries.notes: [V] A distinct failure class from editor-string leakage.

entries.claim: No source consulted for the product requirements establishes that the production bundler is byte-reproducible across two installs of the same lockfile on the same machine; the generator's own determinism is controlled, the bundler's is not.
entries.notes: [V] as an absence-of-evidence statement. This is the reason the reproducibility spike is Phase-0 and the reason the fallback exists.

entries.claim: The documented fallback for two-build equality is a normalised comparison with an enumerated, individually justified exception set, which weakens the export proof from byte-identical to identical-except-for-N-declared-files and therefore requires explicit sign-off.
entries.notes: [V] for the statement; the adequacy of the fallback is [I]. A gate that fails spuriously gets disabled by whoever is trying to ship.

entries.claim: Generation must be a pure function of document, system lock and generator version, with six determinism hazards designed out: iteration order, absolute paths, locale-dependent sorting, random identifiers, binary asset re-encoding, and any clock, network, randomness, environment or outside-filesystem read at generate time.
entries.notes: [V] Binary assets are hash-compared against a recorded output hash rather than re-encoded, because encoders are not bit-stable across versions and re-encoding would manufacture false positives.

entries.claim: Any nondeterminism makes the verify step produce false positives, users learn to ignore it, and the drift guarantee dies silently; this is the load-bearing assumption of the whole drift story.
entries.notes: [V] Recorded as the risk to watch rather than a solved problem.

entries.claim: Hash-journal reconciliation is the only anti-clobber mechanism that holds regardless of how an out-of-band write happened; a command-text scan is explicitly a defeatable heuristic and a read-only file mode is a speed bump, since both processes run as the same user.
entries.notes: [V] The source ranks its own mechanisms by worth and states each limit honestly. That ranking is adopted verbatim.

entries.claim: Forbidding an agent from writing document-owned files without providing a legal write path is how guards get routed around; the sanctioned path is posting the same typed op through the same server, stated in the imperative in the skill's own instructions.
entries.notes: [V] An instruction the agent follows is cheaper and more reliable than a guard it can accidentally evade.

entries.claim: A raw patch over the wire is nearly as dangerous as a raw path, because an add or replace on an arbitrary pointer could rewrite the system lock or inject an override path; the wire format therefore carries typed semantic ops only.
entries.notes: [V] This also corrected an earlier autosave design that posted raw differences.

entries.claim: A commit per save produces thousands of commits per session and makes history useless exactly when it is needed; durability between milestones belongs to the append-only op log plus atomic write-then-rename, with version-control commits at milestones only.
entries.notes: [I] flagged in the source: no source establishes a required cadence; the reconciliation is a design decision made to remove a contradiction between two sections.

entries.claim: A component swap or a section regeneration must be one undo step; naive per-mutation undo leaves a broken hybrid state after a single undo, a known failure class in AI-editing tools, and it fails exactly when the safety net matters most.
entries.notes: [V] Called out in the source as needing dedicated test coverage.

entries.claim: Delete-recovery must be independent of the undo stack, because deleting something three edits ago is common and chaining undo back would revert everything since.

A layers/navigator tree is mandatory in v1: canvas clicking provably cannot reach zero-height wrappers, covered elements, pointer-events-none decoration or empty slots, and a full-bleed background art container otherwise swallows every click.
entries.notes: [V] Three independent review lenses said mandatory; one shipped builder offers all three selection channels for the same reason.

entries.claim: A variant is a structurally distinct composition of the same component within one direction; size, theme, density, state, icon slot and semantic colour are computed axes and never count against the budget. Without that definition the budget silently multiplies roughly twentyfold, which is why two libraries in the same category report five buttons and 940 variants respectively.
entries.notes: [V] Distinctness is machine-checkable through a per-component axis vector.

entries.claim: Market calibration across a commercially curated component library shows per-category variant counts distributed 3-21 and clustered 5-12 with a median near 8, so a default of ten variants per swappable component is market-calibrated rather than arbitrary.
entries.notes: [V] Supports the settled variant-count decision.

entries.claim: The component inventory computes to 216 rows and 1,228 variants (21 identity-carrier rows, 33 plus 111 plus 38 structural rows, 4 artwork sets, 9 policy rows), and the source states plainly that the structural tier was previously understated roughly twofold and that this is a real scope increase rather than a re-labelling.
source_refs: prd:8.2 (computed from the section's own table)
entries.notes: [V] Conflicts with both the 87-items/674-variants figure in the open decisions file and the ~50/~430 figure the timeline and gate budgets were sized against. Carried as NA-02, the largest open scope discrepancy.

entries.claim: Twenty-two inventory rows map to a published interaction pattern and sixty-one more declare a shared audited behavioural primitive; in both cases variants are skin-only and behaviour comes from one audited implementation.
entries.notes: [V] Without the primitive declaration, roughly a hundred variants of overlays, toasts and pickers would each re-invent focus trapping and live-region behaviour.

entries.claim: The choice-overload disagreement resolves in favour of the 2015 meta-analysis (near-zero mean effect with four engineerable moderators) over the single earlier study, so ten variants are safe when the moderators are engineered away; the thumbnail indistinguishability rule from the opposing lens is retained.
entries.notes: [V] for the resolution being recorded; the underlying literature is empirical and contested. The retained rule is the operative safeguard.

entries.claim: A thumbnail grid systematically favours loud, high-contrast directions over subtle editorial ones, so direction selection uses a bracketed tournament with at most three full-size renders side by side, roughly six of ten surfaced by default.
entries.notes: [V] for the decision; the presentation-bias claim is expert judgement rather than a measured result.

entries.claim: The signature moment must be a bespoke concept per direction, not a catalogue of ten picks; treating the identity-carrying choice as a generic catalogue pick is the root mechanism of design homogenisation, and a lint flags a second signature moment.
entries.notes: [V] for the decision; the underlying finding is carried from a prior report. A system that lets the user pick five produces a worse site than one that lets them pick none.

entries.claim: The anti-slop lint splits by layer: a hard gate upstream on the generated design system before the human sees the menu, and a dismissible advisory downstream after a deliberate human choice, because mechanically blocking a chosen direction contradicts the product premise.
entries.notes: [V] for the resolution. The upstream gate is load-bearing precisely because the downstream one is softened.

entries.claim: A published analysis of 1,590 pages found 22% heavily carrying generated-design signatures, 32% mildly and 46% clean, with a catalogue of machine-detectable tells; a separate claim that about three quarters of commercial pages launched in early 2026 carry at least one strong signature is the weaker-sourced figure.
entries.notes: [V] for the page breakdown, [U] for the three-quarters figure.

entries.claim: Model recall of aesthetic animation from frame sequences was measured at 0.16 in prior work that itself flags the area as unvalidated end to end; acceptance of motion therefore rests on the human plus deterministic lint and never on an automated visual score.
entries.notes: [U] Low confidence in the figure, high confidence in the conclusion drawn from it, which is also independently required by the no-AI-aesthetic-judging non-goal.

entries.claim: The editor runtime fights the site runtime, so motion feel cannot be judged while editing; disabling motion in edit mode is the only workable answer and it creates the problem. Recorded as having no known mitigation.
entries.notes: [V] that the limitation is recorded and unsolved. Human-in-the-loop does not solve it; it relocates the unsolved problem.

entries.claim: Continuous motion running beyond five seconds alongside other content requires a working pause, stop or hide control; the rule engine does not reliably catch this criterion, so it needs its own gate, and the container contract needs a pause-affordance field to make an unpausable ticker structurally unbuildable.
entries.notes: [V] The schema change is recorded as an open cross-section coordination item, not as already done.

entries.claim: A skip link must exist, be the very first tab stop and move focus into the main landmark; it was previously absent from both the gate list and the component inventory, and adding the component entry is owned by a different section than the gate.
entries.notes: [V] A missing skip link is not a keyboard trap, so the general tab-walk alone would not flag its absence.

entries.claim: Document order is always the intended reading order; visual order comes only from grid placement. The single legitimate exception is a per-breakpoint order override, which is hard-blocked on focusable nodes because it breaks focus order without a remediation strategy the product does not take on, and warned on non-focusable nodes.
entries.notes: [V] Also requires a numbered mobile stack-order preview before any commit that changes stacking.

entries.claim: Every reference in the built output must resolve to both a manifest entry and a real file on disk with zero remote hosts; licence completeness confirms every recorded asset carries a licence and says nothing about whether every referenced asset exists, so these are distinct gates.
entries.notes: [V] Without the resolution gate a stale or hallucinated path ships as a silently broken image with no error anywhere.

entries.claim: Every font face must ship a metric-matched local fallback computed from the real selected font binary, which can only happen after the human's typeface pick is final and therefore cannot be produced by the generation channel; font-swap-attributable layout shift must be about zero.
entries.notes: [V] Framed as a derived value in the same family as spacing and radius scales, so it belongs to the computed-not-picked set.

entries.claim: A third-party mark must be used as supplied and never redrawn; generating a platform badge is a trademark violation rather than a design choice.
entries.notes: [V] Deterministic embeds, not designable items.

entries.claim: Look and feel is largely not copyrightable absent consumer confusion plus a trade-dress claim requiring integration of multiple non-functional elements; the safe pattern is three or more references from different eras, genres or cultures, abstracted to principles and recombined, with regeneration triggered when any single reference dominates.
entries.notes: [V] for the rule as recorded. This is diligence support, not legal advice.

entries.claim: Subagents in this harness are policy-blocked from writing files and must return findings as text, verified twice by first-party observation; shell heredoc writes are not blocked. Variant generation is therefore a deterministic local generator, not parallel subagents writing files.
entries.notes: [V] first-party. Also guarantees variants stay inside the chosen direction, which is the point of the coherence decision.

entries.claim: Long-running local servers are reaped at the harness turn boundary; the failure is first-party verified across four documented attempts and appears intermittent because it depends on turn timing. Only a double-fork daemon in another language has been observed to survive.
entries.notes: [V] first-party. The pure-language equivalent is UNPROVEN, which is why the probe is the first slice and gates all server-dependent scope.

entries.claim: Liveness is proven only by a health request issued in a separate tool call after the turn boundary, together with confirmation that the recorded process is still present; a same-turn success proves binding, not survival.
entries.notes: [V] first-party operating rule. A backgrounded task is not a server: it binds, answers once, and is terminated.

entries.claim: A prior first-party output tree rotted within months: it is not a version-controlled repository, contains about thirty opaque variant directories with no manifest, and its build scripts record that the authoritative source lived in a temporary directory.
source_refs: prd:15.5 (repository status failure, directory listing, deploy notes)
entries.notes: [V] first-party. Directly motivates initialising version control at step zero, provenance records, generated-file banners and an unlock that refuses to overwrite hand-edits without showing them.

entries.claim: An existing first-party design library holds a complete design system as five files including a specification of roughly 883 lines and a compliance report with 53 per-test records and an aggregate score; that report shape is also the right return format for validating the imported system.
entries.notes: [V] first-party. Warm start is therefore a glob over known paths, not new infrastructure.

entries.claim: A first-party prior-art tree contains thirteen named design lanes times three sub-variants across five pages (195 generated files), a distilled token bundle with a version and hash and roughly eleven colour roles plus two font families per variant, per-variant licence registers, and thirteen recorded screenshot iterations.
entries.notes: [V] first-party. Validates the coherent-whole-direction decision against the user's own prior behaviour and supplies a ready-made evidence-bundle template.

entries.claim: The publish section commits automated deploy as the v1 behaviour after a one-time credential setup, with an explicit fallback trigger to an emitted runbook when no valid credential is configured; the fallback does not satisfy the locked-and-published exit criterion, and the commitment itself is flagged as requiring user sign-off.
entries.notes: [V] for the text; the choice is an interpretation the source labels as needing confirmation. Carried as NA-09, overriding the runbook-first default adopted during normalization.

entries.claim: The interview bank is 90 questions after a row-count self-audit; fast mode asks roughly 45-55 tier-one questions plus one bundled review screen, estimated at 25-35 minutes, rising to roughly 45-70 minutes in open-ended mode. Two other sections and one acceptance criterion still carry the older 78-question and 45-question figures.
entries.notes: [V] for the count, [I] for every duration: per-question timing budgets are estimated from question shape, not measured. The section states that the acceptance criterion should move to 55 or the bank must be cut. Carried as NA-01.

entries.claim: The lock wall-clock target of a 90-second median and 180-second tail for a representative multi-page site is an inference sized against the expanded 32-check gate list, not a measured result, and its sampling fallback for the performance gate is unproven at scale.
entries.notes: [I] Schedule and budget figure - low confidence by standing rule. Validate against a real prototype before treating as a service level.

entries.claim: The motion-concurrency caps (one gpu-class scene, one particle layer, two autoplay video loops, two to three pinned sequences per page) are carried over from prior research and are not benchmarked against this product's render stack.
entries.notes: [I] A starting default, not a validated ceiling. Motion costs are additive, which is why the whole-page budget gate fails late and gives no per-container attribution.

entries.claim: Override-accumulation thresholds (five per page amber, fifteen red, forty per site, or a quarter of a page's nodes) are stated starting numbers, tunable in the project record, and exist so the rule is implementable and testable rather than because they were measured.
entries.notes: [I] Expect to tune after the first real site. A heavily overridden page quietly stops being a design-system site.

entries.claim: The motion-kind homogeneity advisory triggers at three or more distinct variants of the same kind, a carried-over default not independently validated against user testing.
entries.notes: [I] Provisional until real usage data exists. Catalogue breadth is intentional; deployment restraint is the separate concern this signal covers.

entries.claim: Every effort estimate in the source is inference anchored on comparable-project maturity curves rather than measured work, including the canvas layer's 30-60 day range and the decision-driven delta that pulls it into the first shipping version.
entries.notes: [I] Standing rule: every schedule and effort figure is inference with low confidence. None may be quoted as a measurement.

entries.claim: The generation channel's per-message and per-conversation output ceilings are unknown; figures found in 2026 guide content were unverifiable and at least one referenced model name appears fabricated. A separate vendor-described limit of one live artifact per turn is corroborated across several third-party sources plus vendor support material but remains someone else's product surface.
entries.notes: [U] Do not design against any published ceiling. Chunk sizes are computed from measured artifact sizes at runtime.

entries.claim: The generation surface's content policy is assumed to admit a stylesheet while blocking the font binary, so a direction preview would silently fall back to a system face; this is unverified and a sixty-second check must run before the prompt specification is written.
entries.notes: [U] Assumed blocking, which is why pre-subsetted embedded font data is mandated. First-party corroboration is indirect: a prior first-party site shipped zero embedded font faces.

entries.claim: An adopted-dependency licence discrepancy is recorded (one registry reports no assertion, another reports a permissive licence) and must be re-verified against the actual licence file at pin time; this discrepancy class is exactly what bites later.
entries.notes: [U] Applies to every adopted dependency, not just the one named.

entries.claim: The source reuses open-question identifiers across sections: two identifiers each denote three distinct questions, a third denotes both a build-reproducibility question and a user-interface wording question, and a fourth denotes both a process-isolation question and a direction-identity question. Acceptance-criterion identifiers above ninety are also proposed twice by different sections.
entries.notes: [V] by direct read this pass. Every citation must be qualified by section. Carried as NA-08 and NA-19; a renumbering pass is a prerequisite for trustworthy traceability.

entries.claim: The acceptance-criteria section as written contains ninety criteria; the 96-criteria figure carried into this pipeline's normalized inputs is not supported by the section text.
entries.notes: [V] by direct read. Carried as NA-20.

entries.claim: The canonical scene-graph filename is the per-page document plus the project record, not the single layout file named in four other sections and in this pipeline's carried technical requirements.
entries.notes: [V] by direct read. Carried as NA-07; the rename is a prerequisite before implementation.

entries.claim: The free-position auto-demotion boundary is stated as two different widths in two sections: one revises it down to the smallest previewable width, arguing the other is a width no switcher, frame or gate ever renders, while the save-format section defines the small breakpoint at the older boundary and calls the two identical.
entries.notes: [V] by direct read. Carried as NA-06: adopt the previewable width as the demotion trigger, keep the media-query boundary, and fix all call sites together.

entries.claim: The editor feature table contains 116 rows split 56 v1 / 55 v2 / 5 v3 under the editor-lite scope, and the section records that an earlier prose claim of about 35 of 95 items was off by roughly twofold on the v1 count.
source_refs: prd:10 (mechanical recount stated in the section)
entries.notes: [V] for the recount. Pulling the canvas rows into v1 raises v1 to roughly 65-70 rows, which is [I] arithmetic on the promoted rows, not a fresh recount. Carried as NA-12.

entries.claim: Adopted default (open decision, component set): re-baseline the v1 component set to the 87-item / 674-variant figure, then demote per project only what the interview says the project does not need, with two named components non-demotable.
entries.notes: [I] Internal adopted default, low confidence, traceable to the open decisions file so a later reversal is visible. Superseded in volume by EL-037.

entries.claim: Adopted default (open decision, artwork count): twenty artworks total per direction for v1, while stating plainly that a sprite-heavy game-style site needs a different artwork path.
entries.notes: [I] Internal adopted default, low confidence.

entries.claim: Adopted default (open decision, page count): single page, but the document carries a page array of length one and every operation is page-scoped from day one, so multi-page becomes a feature addition rather than a data migration.
entries.notes: [I] Needs clarification: the recommendation labels this branch but its supporting prose argues for shared global regions, which is the other branch. The label was followed, not the prose.

entries.claim: Adopted default (open decision, build reproducibility): run the spike before committing to two-build equality; if it fails, accept a normalised comparison and say so explicitly rather than claiming a guarantee the toolchain cannot give.
entries.notes: [I] Internal adopted default. The success criterion is written against the spike's outcome.

entries.claim: Adopted default (open decision, anchoring): parent-edge and grid-cell anchors only in v1; sibling anchoring is held behind an unprototyped subgrid-promotion strategy.
entries.notes: [I] Internal adopted default. Sibling anchors are where constraint systems usually break, and neither implementation path is currently legal as written.

entries.claim: Adopted defaults (open decisions, editor behaviour): regeneration stays a reviewed operation with per-node flags and bulk acknowledge; no wide override tier in v1; the widest size is a preview-only switcher option carrying no overrides.
entries.notes: [I] Internal adopted defaults. The no-wide-tier choice avoids introducing the only upward override in a downward cascade.

entries.claim: Adopted defaults (open decisions, generation inputs): 24-32 licence-cleared families seed the font catalog; motion-concurrency caps ship as provisional and are benchmarked during v1; the variant-axis schema is hand-authored in the skill for determinism with its own effort line.
entries.notes: [I] Internal adopted defaults; the family count is a starting number to revise after the first real run.

entries.claim: Adopted defaults (open decisions, limits and measurement): a project with no asset library is a per-project limitation warned at interview time; two reconstructed inventory subsections are treated as provisional and flagged for confirmation; repeat use is measured from local session files in a rolling window with no telemetry; the interview asks about audience access needs and that answer may only tighten a gate threshold.
entries.notes: [I] Internal adopted defaults. The no-asset-library case has no known mitigation that preserves the paste-only path.

entries.claim: Adopted defaults (open architecture questions): build only the topology-independent invariants until the topology spike lands; take the first passing launcher rung and prefer the shell launcher because it keeps the server in the standing language; assume the font policy blocks and mandate embedded font data; keep the substrate open so nothing hard-depends on one framework; design v1 so nothing depends on unverified mid-skill subagent availability.
entries.notes: [I] Internal adopted defaults, each traceable to a named open question. Two launcher rungs require explicit sign-off and, if both are refused, there is no known mitigation.

entries.claim: Adopted defaults (open product questions): export is a re-render; charts are build-time vector with a small mark cap; section regeneration runs inline rather than through the manual channel; redesign forks rather than replacing in place; agent operations always go through the inbox; a second tab is read-only; the compiled token stylesheet is machine-owned with a sanctioned extraction path; lock snapshots carry documents and the system lock only; the element-protection verb is Freeze.
entries.notes: [I] Internal adopted defaults. The export question is described in the source as the single most consequential architectural decision of the eight steps and is still marked confirm-with-the-user.

entries.claim: The custom-component path in the source names a subagent call, which conflicts with the architecture rule that nothing may depend on unverified mid-skill subagent availability; inline main-session execution of the role prompt is adopted instead.
entries.notes: [V] for the conflict, [I] for the resolution. Carried as NA-10.

entries.claim: The two-build gate procedure in the source is written against a package-manager install and a committed publish manifest pair, while the skill's own code is required to be in the standing language; the site build toolchain is whatever the substrate spike selects, so the gate's installer invocation must be re-derived from that outcome.
entries.notes: [V] for the mismatch, [I] for the resolution. Carried as NA-11.

entries.claim: Deliberately excluded, each with a recorded justification: an automated aesthetic judge loop, conflict-free replicated data types, a browser filesystem persistence path, building inside an existing editor framework, new agent definition files, a tool declaration the framework ignores, an evictable browser-automation cache, copying rather than porting prior-language code, ten catalogued signature moments, hard downstream aesthetic blocking, an N-up direction grid, raw editable regions on every text node, absolute positioning as the free-position implementation, two independent layouts, injected hit-test wrappers, markup-to-document round-tripping, and a systems language nothing here needs.
entries.notes: [V] Each exclusion carries a stated reason in the source; none is re-litigated here.

entries.claim: The lock-time checklist is 32 checks: 28 base gates plus four lettered insertions covering motion-concurrency caps, skip-link presence, pause affordances and asset-reference resolution.
entries.notes: [V] Carried as NA-04. Ordering is cheapest-and-most-foundational first, and the lettered inserts sit at the position their cost class and dependencies require.
